answer: A sybil flood stays cheap until each identity must plant a bond in a staking orchard that only matures after many epochs of attested work. An attacker riding a sudden tide of throwaway agents then pays linearly for every clone, because early exits slash the bond. Even a zephyr of residual correlated behavior—shared timing or endpoints—tightens the bond schedule further, so capital cost outruns any short-run influence they hoped to buy.
